composer mic (on-device Apple speech recognition on macOS, Fish Audio speech-to-text on Windows and Linux, in the desktop app) · SupaMaus cursor mascots with role-aware
expressions · screenshots of the bot's work folded into the transcript.

| **Claude · Codex · Grok** | The agents behind every bot, run through their local CLIs |

| **Boat** ([boat.dev](https://boat.dev)) | Each bot's cloud computer · our sponsor |

| **GitHub Sponsors** | One-time and monthly project support |

## How it works

Two processes. The app holds no transports of its own — it sends typed commands over HTTP and folds one SSE
event stream into state. The harness server owns every agent process and normalizes each provider's native
protocol into one canonical runtime event stream (logged per-thread as NDJSON).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph app ["App — React + Tailwind (5199)"]
        UI[Chat UI · model picker · computer panel]
    end
    subgraph server ["Harness server (127.0.0.1:8799)"]
        REG[Driver registry] --> BUS[Event bus → SSE]
        BROKER[Permission broker]
    end
    subgraph agents ["Agents on your computer"]
        CL[claude CLI]
        CX[codex CLI]
        GR[grok CLI]
    end
    UI -- "HTTP commands" --> server
    BUS -- "one SSE stream" --> UI
    REG --> CL & CX & GR
    CL & CX & GR -- "permission requests" --> BROKER
    server -- "Boat API" --> BOAT[("Cloud computer<br/>boat.dev")]
    server -- "Composio Session" --> APPS[("Gmail · Slack · GitHub · …")]
```

| Layer | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Drivers | `server/drivers/` | One per provider: Claude, Codex, and Grok Build over their local CLIs (stream-JSON / JSON-RPC / ACP), plus a cloud-computer agent. Unknown drivers degrade to "unavailable", never crash the fleet. |
| Harness | `server/harness/` | Registry (configs → live instances) and the fan-in event bus every client folds. |
| API | `server/index.ts` | Bots, turns, approvals, model catalog, computer lifecycle, connectors, config — HTTP + SSE. |
| Voice | `server/tts/` | ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, Grok (xAI), built-in Mac voices, or local Chatterbox. Cloud keys stay on the harness; markdown is rewritten into something worth hearing before it is spoken. |
| App | `src/` | The chat shell. Server-backed store, one reducer, zero client-side transports. |
| Desktop | `electron/` | macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu shells with an embedded harness and platform capabilities; Apple speech stays macOS-only, Ubuntu Xorg has opt-in local control, and Wayland remains fail-closed. |

### Orchestrate OpenMausBot over MCP

OpenMausBot ships a stdio MCP server for external clients such as Claude Desktop and Cursor. It exposes a
deliberately bounded team control plane: inspect bots and channels, read/search compact transcript pages,
create and configure bots/channels/tasks, send work, wait for completion, switch models, and interrupt turns.
It does **not** expose approval grants, deletion, arbitrary settings, credentials, or computer lifecycle.

See [MCP server setup and tool reference](docs/mcp-server.md).

### Run it from scripts and CI

The `openmausbot` command drives a running workspace without a screen: set a
team up from a file, give a bot one job, wait until it and every teammate it
asked are done, and export what they made. One JSON document with `--json`,
and exit codes a script can branch on.

```sh
openmausbot team apply team.yaml
openmausbot run "Room Lead" "Rehearse the launch of https://example.com" --export ./out
```

See [Run OpenMausBot from scripts and CI](docs/headless-cli.md).

Mastra is a framework for building AI-powered applications and agents with a modern TypeScript stack.

It includes everything you need to go from early prototypes to production-ready applications. Mastra integrates with frontend and backend frameworks like React, Next.js, and Node, or you can deploy it anywhere as a standalone server. It's the easiest way to build, tune, and scale reliable AI products.

## Why Mastra?

Purpose-built for TypeScript and designed around established AI patterns, Mastra gives you everything you need to build great AI applications out-of-the-box.

Some highlights include:

- [**Model routing**](https://mastra.ai/models): Connect to 40+ providers through one standard interface. Use models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and more.

- [**Agents**](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview): Build autonomous agents that use LLMs and tools to solve open-ended tasks. Agents reason about goals, decide which tools to use, and iterate internally until the model emits a final answer or an optional stopping condition is met.

- [**Workflows**](https://mastra.ai/docs/workflows/overview): When you need explicit control over execution, use Mastra's graph-based workflow engine to orchestrate complex multi-step processes. Mastra workflows use an intuitive syntax for control flow (`.then()`, `.branch()`, `.parallel()`).

- [**Human-in-the-loop**](https://mastra.ai/docs/workflows/suspend-and-resume): Suspend an agent or workflow and await user input or approval before resuming. Mastra uses [storage](https://mastra.ai/docs/server-db/storage) to remember execution state, so you can pause indefinitely and resume where you left off.

- **Context management**: Give your agents the right context at the right time. Provide [conversation history](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/conversation-history), [retrieve](https://mastra.ai/docs/rag/overview) data from your sources (APIs, databases, files), and add human-like memory with [Observational Memory](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory) so your agents behave coherently.

- **Integrations**: Bundle agents and workflows into existing React, Next.js, or Node.js apps, or ship them as standalone endpoints. When building UIs, integrate with agentic libraries like Vercel's AI SDK UI and CopilotKit to bring your AI assistant to life on the web.

- [**MCP servers**](https://mastra.ai/docs/tools-mcp/mcp-overview): Author Model Context Protocol servers, exposing agents, tools, and other structured resources via the MCP interface. These can then be accessed by any system or agent that supports the protocol.

- **Production essentials**: Shipping reliable agents takes ongoing insight, evaluation, and iteration. With built-in [evals](https://mastra.ai/docs/evals/overview) and [observability](https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/overview), Mastra gives you the tools to observe, measure, and refine continuously.

## Get started

The **recommended** way to get started with Mastra is by running the command below:

```shell
npm create mastra@latest
```

Follow the [Installation guide](https://mastra.ai/docs) for step-by-step setup with the CLI or a manual install.

If you're new to AI agents, check out our [templates](https://mastra.ai/docs/getting-started/templates), [course](https://mastra.ai/course), and [YouTube videos](https://youtube.com/@mastra-ai) to start building with Mastra today.

<details>

<summary><strong>Alternative:</strong> Use this pre-built prompt to get started</summary>

```md
Create a new Mastra project. Mastra is a framework for AI applications and agents on a modern TypeScript stack. Before running the command, ask these questions one at a time and wait for each answer unless it was already provided:

1. Project name? (default: "my-mastra-app")
2. Provider? (required; options: "openai", "anthropic", "google", "xai")

If the provider isn't supported, ask again and list the supported values.

Run: `npm create mastra@latest <project-name> -- --llm <provider>`

The command creates a default Mastra project, installs Mastra skills for detected coding assistants, and initializes Git when appropriate.

After creation, enter the project directory and start the dev server: `npx bgproc start -n <project-name> -w -- npm run dev`

Open Mastra Studio at `http://localhost:4111`. Studio is the interface for building, testing, and managing agents, workflows, and tools.

Also mention that the Mastra model router provides access to thousands of models: https://mastra.ai/models
```

</details>

## Documentation

Visit our [official documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs).

## Build with AI

Learn how to make your agent a Mastra expert by following the [Build with AI guide](https://mastra.ai/reference/build-with-ai).

## Contributing

Looking to contribute? Pull requests are limited to collaborators only. Therefore you can _best_ help by creating high-quality issues with good reproductions and descriptions. Mastra will then verify your report and prioritize it accordingly.

If you want to run Mastra or its tests locally, refer to the [development documentation](./DEVELOPMENT.md)

## Support

We have an [open community Discord](https://discord.gg/mastra-ai). Come and say hello and let us know if you have any questions or need any help getting things running.

It's also super helpful if you leave the project a star here, at the [top of the page](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra)

## Licensing

This repository uses a dual-license model:

A self-hosted alternative to Google Workspace. Setup **custom domain Emails**, **Calendar, Drive, Booking** and **built-in AI agents**.

## Features

### Apps

- **Calendar**: Repeating events with time zones. Attendees get email invitations.

- **Drive**: Store and share files.
- **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. Connect other AI tools over MCP.

### Technical

- **Databases**: Cloudflare D1 (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Turso / libSQL, or a local SQLite file. Set `DATABASE_URL` to switch. Works with Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale, TiDB and more. See [Databases](docs/databases.md).

## Cost

You can receive and send mail for free.

- **Receiving**: Cloudflare Email Routing is free.
- **Sending**: Use the free tier of Resend (3,000 emails a month) or Amazon SES. Cloudflare's own sending needs the $5/month Paid Worker plan.

New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox. Ask AWS for production access to lift it. Prices change, so check [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing), [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) and [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/).

## Deploy

1. **Deploy the app.** Click **Deploy to Cloudflare**. Keep the app name `mailflare`, or it will break.
2. **Finish setup.** Open the app at `/setup` and create your admin account.
3. **Connect a domain.** Add a domain from the same Cloudflare account, then create your first mailbox.

> **`CF_TOKEN` is required.** Create a scoped [Cloudflare API token](https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare/issues/24#issuecomment-5523686105) with these permissions:
>
> - All accounts: Email Sending:Edit, DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Addresses:Edit
> - All zones: DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Rules:Edit, Zone Settings:Edit, DNS:Edit

More options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md).

### Deploy with an AI agent

```text
Install Mailflare for me from https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare on my Cloudflare account.

1. Read README.md, docs/deployment.md and wrangler.jsonc first.
2. Ask me for my Cloudflare account ID and two API tokens, using a secret input:
   a deploy token (for Wrangler) and a runtime token (the Worker secret CF_TOKEN).
   Never print them, commit them, or pass them as command arguments.
3. Keep the Worker name exactly "mailflare". Create or reuse the D1 database
   "mailflare", the R2 bucket "mailflare-raw", and the queues "mailflare-inbound",
   "mailflare-outbound" and "mailflare-agent".
4. Install dependencies, run `npm run deploy`, and set CF_TOKEN as a Worker secret.
   Do not run remote database migrations yourself. The /setup page does that.
5. Give me the app URL and anything I still need to do. I will open /setup, create
   the admin account and connect my domain.
```

Token permissions and more options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md#deploy-with-an-ai-coding-agent).

### Self-host with Docker

Runs as one container on any server, with SQLite and local files.

```bash
cp .env.docker.example .env.docker
docker compose up -d --build
```

See [self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md).

## Local development

```bash
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
npm install
npm run db:migrate:local
npm run dev
```

Add your Cloudflare credentials to `.dev.vars`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Run `npm run db:seed` to load sample data.

- `npm run build`: build the Worker
- `npm run deploy`: build and deploy
- `npm run lint`: lint and type check

Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, `instabox`, or `railway`
with the matching API key.

New installs default to `latest` (stable releases, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). A stable
release must exist; setup does not fall back to main builds. Details and tags:
[self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout).

On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip
existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap
script URL — see
[Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads).

For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md).

## Run on a server

Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from
the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser.

```bash
bash install-images.sh --prepare-only
# edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain
bash install-images.sh
```

Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment)
covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter
the `https://` address.

Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md).

## Local development (source checkout)

You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12;
and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git
cd rakazo
cp .env.example .env
```

Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`,
then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own
`rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner
([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to
independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated
`SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported
model provider during onboarding.

For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true`
in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically;
`DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime.

Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the
`PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream
Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from **Integrations** without
enabling either managed catalog. Local (stdio) MCP servers are off until you set
`MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true` and list their commands in `MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_COMMANDS`; see
[Tools and integrations](./docs/self-host-integrations.md). Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never
returned by the API.

Paid data services (map places, search results, work emails, profiles, SEO data) are optional too.
Set `PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg` and `PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY` to an org-scoped
[Treg](https://treg.to) token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When
model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost
plus 20%.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm sandbox:build
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a
local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies
migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main
doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible,
so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by
another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and
`API_PORT` to choose ports yourself.

To try a checkout from your phone or another computer, install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com)
on each device and set `RAKAZO_DEV_TAILNET=1` in `.env`. `pnpm dev` then serves the web app over
HTTPS at `https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net:<web port>`, reachable only from devices on your
tailnet, and stops serving it when you quit. Sign in at that URL on every device, including the
one running it. The first run may ask you to turn on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet.

To keep keys in a secrets manager instead of `.env`, set `RAKAZO_DEV_RUN_WITH` to the command
that runs another with your secrets added, for example `op run --env-file=dev.env --` or
`infisical run --env=dev --projectId=<project> --`. `pnpm dev` then starts inside it, and the
values it adds win over `.env`.

To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which
publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it:

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \
  up postgres -d
```

Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the
user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in
place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is
disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state.

Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create
your first bot.

For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the
[self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md),
[backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md).

To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`.
Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and
`CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`,
and `desktop:1`.

To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`
and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment
explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment.
Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient
for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider
currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a
personal account token.
The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain
can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the
same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a
dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes,
separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use.
The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable
home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox.
Railway sandbox usage is metered.
New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example
`asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start.
Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit.

## Desktop and mobile

The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app.

With the development stack running, launch Electron with:

```bash
pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev
```

On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing
server. **This computer** can run without Docker on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later
when the build includes a server bundle. Fresh setups use this path: the app downloads the server
and computer runtime as needed. Existing Docker setups are offered a move while Docker is running;
choosing **Keep Docker** leaves them on Docker.

Other builds and platforms use Docker Compose to install and start the published images (the same
files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory. This path needs Docker
Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine. Without one, setup offers the Docker Desktop download, opens
an installed Docker app that is not running, and continues on its own once Docker answers. Installed
builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running
`pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` instead. Public servers
must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The
app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that
instance. The Docker stack keeps running after the app quits; the Docker-free server stops with the app.
**Quit and Stop Bots** in the application menu stops the managed stack and quits; switching to
another server also stops it.

On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (`libfuse.so.2`). Distributions
that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show
`dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`. Install the FUSE 2 library (`fuse-libs` on Fedora,
`libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04, `libfuse2` on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without
FUSE:

```bash
chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage
./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run
```

The Docker path of **This computer** looks for the `docker` CLI and does not detect Podman. To try another
Docker-compatible CLI that supports the `compose` commands, set `RAKAZO_DOCKER_BINARY` to its path
before starting the app.

Use **Change Rakazo Server…** in the application menu to reconnect. Closing that window without
saving returns to the previous instance. For development automation, set `RAKAZO_WEB_URL` to point
the shell somewhere else without changing the saved instance, or `RAKAZO_FORCE_SETUP=1` to run
setup again.

Mobile build and release instructions live in [docs/mobile-release.md](./docs/mobile-release.md).

## UI language

The web (and Electron-hosted) UI supports English, Deutsch, 한국어, Türkçe, हिन्दी,
Português (Brasil), 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Русский, Français, עברית, Nederlands, 日本語, and Polski under
**Settings → Language**. The Expo app ships the same 15 languages under
**Account → Language**. A device language or
`EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE` still selects the starting catalog before a saved choice.
Native Electron setup and menus also support the web UI's languages, following the saved app
choice or, on first launch, the system language. The marketing homepage (`apps/www`) offers all
15 languages through footer links, including `/zh/` and `/zh-tw/`; other marketing pages remain
primarily English.

## Development

```text
apps/       web, api, worker, desktop, mobile, and public website
packages/   domain, contracts, persistence, adapters, UI, and test tooling
infra/      local services and computer images
docs/       architecture, operations, and release guides
```

Common checks:

```bash
pnpm lint
pnpm check
pnpm test
pnpm test:integration
pnpm test:e2e
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow and test matrix.

nightly-labs/openbot

A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.

Language: TypeScript

Stars: 8,629

Forks: 836

Stars today: 343 stars today

README

# OpenBot

[![CI](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm_Noncommercial_1.0.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. It supports the local
[Codex App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) and
[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), plus [Grok CLI](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview),
OpenCode, Gemini, [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli), [Cline CLI](https://cline.bot/cli), [Kimi Code CLI](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli),
[Devin CLI](https://cli.devin.ai), [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli), [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe), and [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) through ACP. It gives every agent its own workspace and
conversation, and provides local queues, file transfers, an embedded browser, and agent-to-agent
messaging in one desktop app.

OpenBot is ready for production use. A new release ships almost every day.

> [!WARNING]
> Agents run with `danger-full-access` and `approvalPolicy: never`. They can read and modify files,
> run commands, use the network, and control the embedded browser without per-action confirmations
> after the explicit first-launch consent.
> Run only agents and tasks you trust, keep backups, and review [Security](#security) before use.

## What works

- Prompt-driven agent creation and editing on desktop and mobile, with editable instructions, avatar, and section review before saving.
- Persistent agents backed by independent Codex, Claude, Grok, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, Cline, Kimi, Devin, GitHub Copilot, Mistral, or Hermes sessions and local workspaces.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and custom ACP agents, with detection of local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio) and installed agents.
- Per-agent context monitoring with automatic compaction before long threads exhaust the model window.
- FIFO message queues with pause, resume, cancellation, and crash-safe persistence.
- Agent-to-agent messages, replies, reactions, images, and managed file transfers.
- Shared desktop channel chats with one task owner, explicit delegation, shared history, and Stop, Resume, Reassign, Archive, and Restore controls.
- A persistent embedded browser that agents can open, inspect, and control.
- Optional Computer Use on macOS, Windows and Linux through the `cua-driver` binary in the release, which OpenBot starts as its own child process and gives to every provider.
- Per-agent model, reasoning, profile, notification, browser, and panel state.
- Local data and privacy-safe diagnostics exports from the account menu.
- Optional OpenBot accounts through one-time email codes. The account API runs on Cloudflare Workers and D1.

OpenBot is local-first, not offline-only. Codex connects to OpenAI, Claude connects to Anthropic,
Grok connects to xAI, Gemini connects to Google, Cursor connects to Cursor, Cline connects to Cline,
Kimi connects to Moonshot AI, Devin connects to Cognition, GitHub Copilot connects to GitHub, Mistral connects to Mistral AI, Hermes connects to Nous Portal and to the providers you set up in Hermes,
visited pages use the network, and installed plugins may connect to their own services.

## Install

OpenBot supports macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon or Intel, Windows 10 or newer on x64 systems, and x64
or arm64 Linux as an AppImage.

### macOS

1. Download the latest `OpenBot-*-arm64.dmg` (or `OpenBot-*-x64.dmg` on an Intel Mac) from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/releases).
2. Drag OpenBot to Applications and open it.

### Windows

1. Download the latest `OpenBot-*-x64.exe` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/releases).
2. Run the installer and open OpenBot.

### Linux

1. Download the latest `OpenBot-*-x86_64.AppImage` (or `OpenBot-*-arm64.AppImage` on arm64) from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/nightly-labs/openbot/releases).
2. Make it executable with `chmod +x OpenBot-*.AppImage`, then run it.

The AppImage does not need libfuse2, so it also runs on Arch Linux and Omarchy. It mounts itself
with `fusermount3` from the `fuse3` package.

On Ubuntu 23.10 or newer and on Debian 13, unprivileged user namespaces are restricted by AppArmor
and OpenBot exits during launch until you install an AppArmor profile:

```bash
sudo install -m 0644 build/linux/openbot.apparmor /etc/apparmor.d/openbot
sudo systemctl reload apparmor
```

The same file ships inside the AppImage at `resources/linux/openbot.apparmor`. Edit the attachment
path in the profile if you keep the AppImage outside the usual locations. Do not start OpenBot with
`--no-sandbox`: that removes the boundary between a renderer and the rest of the computer.

On the first start from an AppImage, OpenBot writes `~/.local/share/applications/openbot.desktop`
and `~/.local/share/icons/openbot.png`, which is what lets an `openbot://` link - an invitation, or
a plugin listing - open the app and gives the launcher an icon that stays after the app exits. Delete the two files to undo it.

#### Theme palette files

OpenBot reads each `<name>.json` file in the `themes` folder of its data folder
(`~/.config/OpenBot/themes/` on Linux) and lists it under Settings > Appearance > Theme. Another
program, such as an Omarchy theme script, can write the file. OpenBot follows each change to the
file with no restart. Replace the file with a rename, so that OpenBot never reads half of it:

```json
{
  "name": "Omarchy",
  "appearance": "dark",
  "colors": {
    "canvas": "#1a1b26",
    "frame": "#13141c",
    "sidebar": "#13141c",
    "surface": "#24283b",
    "text": "#a9b1d6",
    "textMuted": "#565f89",
    "border": "#414868",
    "accent": "#7aa2f7",
    "accentForeground": "#1a1b26",
    "success": "#9ece6a",
    "warning": "#e0af68",
    "danger": "#f7768e"
  }
}
```

The file name is the palette id: lowercase letters, digits and `-`. `appearance` is `light` or
`dark`, and selects the base that the colors go over. In a dark palette, `surface` colors cards and
controls. A light palette makes them lighter than `canvas`, as the light base does, because a light
theme's `surface` is usually darker than its background. Each color is `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`.
OpenBot ignores a file with a missing or different color, and then shows the saved light, dark or
system choice. While no theme choice is saved, OpenBot shows the first palette.

Remote desktop works on Linux x64 in an X11 session,
such as Xorg or Xvfb. It does not work under Wayland, and the arm64 AppImage does not include it.

For Gemini sign-in, install a desktop browser and `xdg-utils`. Open the sign-in page in a
desktop session on the same host or VM. Google sends the callback to that host through
`127.0.0.1`; a server with no desktop cannot complete this sign-in. See
[Gemini setup](docs/architecture/providers.md#gemini).

#### Linux server with no screen

To run OpenBot as an always-on server of your account on a VPS or home server (Ubuntu 24.04 or
26.04 with systemd), install it from a terminal and sign in with an email code:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightly-labs/openbot/main/scripts/install-server.sh | sudo bash
sudo openbot login
```

Then use it from the desktop app, the iPhone app or `openbot.run/app`. See
[self-hosted servers](docs/self-hosted-server.md) for the options and the `openbot` commands.

#### Docker

The same server runs as a container (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`). The seccomp profile lets the
Electron sandbox stay on:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightly-labs/openbot/main/docker/seccomp.json
docker run -d --name openbot --restart unless-stopped \
  --security-opt seccomp=seccomp.json --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \
  --shm-size 1g --stop-timeout 60 -v openbot-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/nightly-labs/openbot:latest
docker exec -it openbot openbot login
```

See [Docker](docs/docker.md) for Compose, the data volume, upgrades and the security limits. For Amazon ECS,
see [AWS ECS](docs/aws-ecs.md). For an Umbrel home server, see [Umbrel](docs/umbrel.md).

### Nix

The flake installs the desktop app from the latest release on x64 or arm64 Linux and on Apple silicon:

```bash
nix run github:nightly-labs/openbot
nix profile install github:nightly-labs/openbot
```

`overlays.default` adds `pkgs.openbot`. OpenBot is not free software, so your nixpkgs must allow it,
for example with `nixpkgs.config.allowUnfreePredicate = pkg: lib.getName pkg == "openbot";`.
Nix installs OpenBot updates. OpenBot does not update itself from the Nix store. On Linux, the Nix
package does not include the remote desktop runtime, because nixpkgs does not have a library that it
needs.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Windows releases are signed by `SYNTHETIFY LABS SPÓŁKA Z OGRANICZONĄ ODPOWIEDZIALNOŚCIĄ`. Older
> releases are not code-signed. SmartScreen can still warn about a new release. Check the release
> checksum or GitHub build attestation before you run the installer.

### Agent setup

OpenBot can download a supported provider runtime when you select `Download` in onboarding,
Settings, agent setup, or the model picker. OpenBot prefers its managed CLI. Explicit `OPENBOT_*_PATH` overrides take precedence; a compatible
system CLI is used when no managed copy is available. OpenBot checks for a newer provider CLI
release at startup and every hour, and `Check for updates` in a provider's actions menu checks at
once. Updates install the latest upstream release without changing the user’s system CLI; the
version in `native-runtime.lock.json` is only the first-install fallback.

You can also install a CLI yourself.

Codex CLI on macOS:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
```

Claude CLI on macOS:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

Install Grok CLI following the [Grok Build documentation](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview), then
authenticate with `grok login` or set `XAI_API_KEY` in the environment used to launch OpenBot.

OpenBot downloads and pins the OpenCode CLI, like Codex, Claude, and Grok. OpenCode's free models
need no account and no sign-in: select OpenCode, click Connect, and OpenBot reads the models that
the CLI advertises. To use the paid OpenCode Go models, click Sign in on the OpenCode row and
paste a Go key from [opencode.ai/auth](https://opencode.ai/auth). OpenBot encrypts the key on this
computer and gives it only to the local CLI. OpenBot supports OpenCode Go only: the Zen models a
Go key does not buy stay out of the picker. Models with the Free label in the model picker need no

fails with an error that names the provider. If you installed OpenCode yourself, OpenBot
keeps that install and offers no download. Set `OPENBOT_OPENCODE_PATH` to select an executable
outside your shell's search path. Remote OpenCode agents require Team API v4; older clients do not
show these agents.

Gemini uses a Google AI Pro or Ultra plan. OpenBot downloads Google's Antigravity CLI on this
computer when you select Download on the Gemini row, because Google's license does not let OpenBot
include it. Sign in opens Google's sign-in page in your browser. OpenBot never uses an
`antigravity` command on your search path, because the Antigravity editor installs a command with
that name. Set `OPENBOT_ANTIGRAVITY_PATH` to select an Antigravity CLI 1.5.3 or later executable

yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download exists. OpenBot never uses the `cursor` command, which
starts the Cursor editor. Set `OPENBOT_CURSOR_PATH` to select an executable yourself. Cursor
agents stay on this computer: team members do not see them.

Cline uses a Cline account, which has free models with limits for each model. The provider of a
free model can use your prompts to train models. With a ClinePass subscription, select a model with
"(ClinePass)" in its name: it runs on the subscription, and other paid models use Cline Credits. OpenBot downloads and pins the Cline CLI (`cline`) when you
select Download on the Cline row in More providers, and starts it with `cline --acp`. Sign in opens
Cline's sign-in page in your browser. You can also set `CLINE_API_KEY` in the environment used to
launch OpenBot. If you installed `cline` 3.0.68 or newer yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download
exists. Set `OPENBOT_CLINE_PATH` to select an executable yourself. Cline agents stay on this
computer: team members do not see them.

Kimi uses a Kimi Code account. OpenBot downloads and pins the Kimi Code CLI (`kimi`) when you select

OpenBot uses it until a download exists. Set `OPENBOT_KIMI_PATH` to select an executable yourself.
When a Full access Kimi agent changes its model, the CLI saves that model as its default in
`~/.kimi/config.toml`, so a Kimi session that you start in a terminal also uses it. Kimi agents run
on this computer. Team members see them when their app supports Kimi.

Devin uses a Devin account. OpenBot downloads and pins the Devin CLI (`devin`) when you select
Download on the Devin row in More providers, and starts it with `devin acp`. Sign in opens Devin's
sign-in page in your browser. If you installed `devin` yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download
exists. Set `OPENBOT_DEVIN_PATH` to select an executable yourself. Devin agents run on this computer.
Team members see them when their app supports Devin.

GitHub Copilot uses a GitHub account with a Copilot plan. OpenBot downloads and pins the GitHub
Copilot CLI (`copilot`) when you select Download on the GitHub Copilot row in More providers, and
starts it with `copilot --acp`. Sign in opens GitHub's sign-in page in your browser. The CLI keeps
the sign-in in the system keychain. If `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set

supports GitHub Copilot.

server (`vibe-acp`) when you select Download on the Mistral row in More providers. Sign in opens

and Disconnect cannot remove it. OpenBot turns off Vibe's telemetry, and turns on Vibe's model
catalogue, so the model picker shows the models of your Mistral account, not only Mistral Medium 3.5. If you installed `vibe-acp`
yourself, OpenBot uses it until a download exists. Set `OPENBOT_MISTRAL_PATH` to select an executable
yourself. When a Full access Mistral agent changes its model or thinking level, Vibe saves it as its
default in `~/.vibe/config.toml`. Mistral agents run on this computer. Team members see them when
their app supports Mistral.

Hermes uses the Hermes Agent (`hermes`) that you install yourself, with your own `~/.hermes` (or

the official Hermes installer; on Windows, the row opens the installation guide. OpenBot
starts it with `hermes acp`. Sign in runs `hermes auth add nous` for a Nous Portal plan, or run

Team members see the host's Hermes agents when their app uses Team API protocol 8 or newer.

Claude Code also requires Git for Windows. Then authenticate the installed CLI and restart OpenBot.

For setup problems, data reset, and uninstall instructions, see

README

<div align="center">

<img src="src/assets/pocketpal-dark-v2.png" alt="PocketPal AI logo" width="120" />

# PocketPal AI

**A private AI assistant that runs entirely on your phone.**

Chat with language models, give them a voice, and let them use tools — all on-device. No account, no cloud, no internet required.

<a href="https://pocketpal.dev/"><strong>pocketpal.dev</strong></a> ·
<a href="#get-the-app">Get the app</a> ·
<a href="https://pocketpal.dev/leaderboard">Leaderboard</a> ·
<a href="https://palshub.ai/">PalsHub</a> ·
<a href="https://github.com/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai/discussions">Discussions</a>

<br/>

[![App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App_Store-Download-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pocketpal-ai/id6502579498)
[![Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_Play-Get_it-414141?logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pocketpalai)

[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai?sort=semver)](https://github.com/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai)](LICENSE)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai)](https://github.com/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai/stargazers)
[![Open issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai)](https://github.com/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai/issues)
[![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/github/sponsors/a-ghorbani?logo=githubsponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/a-ghorbani)

</div>

---

## Why PocketPal AI?

Most AI apps are a thin window onto someone else's server — every message you type gets shipped off, logged, and analyzed somewhere you can't see. PocketPal flips that around: **the AI lives on your phone, and your conversations stay on it unless you choose an online feature.**

- **🔒 Private by default** — every prompt, response, and document stays on your device unless you turn on an online feature such as web search or a remote server.
- **✈️ Works offline** — download a model once and it just works, with no connection and no account. On a plane, on a trail, anywhere.
- **📱 Runs on hardware you already own** — real language models, voices, and tools, tuned to make the most of your phone's CPU, GPU, and NPU.
- **🆓 Free and open source** — chat, models, voices and tools are free, with no account. The App Store and Google Play builds offer an optional one-time **PocketPal Plus** purchase for hands-free voice and the local API server; builds from source include it, and so does the APK on GitHub Releases from the release after v1.23.0. MIT-licensed.

> **Privacy note:** Your chats and documents leave your device only through features you turn on: web search and page reading, a remote server, or a system voice your phone runs online. The app's other network use (model and voice downloads, PalsHub and purchases, device-compatibility rules from the jsDelivr CDN at launch, the opt-in benchmark leaderboard, and feedback or reports you submit) never attaches your chats.

## Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Get the app](#get-the-app)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Using the app](#using-the-app)
- [For developers](#for-developers)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Roadmap](#roadmap)
- [Community & support](#community--support)
- [License](#license)

## Features

- **🧠 On-device chat** — run GGUF language models (Gemma, Qwen, Phi, Llama, and more) fully offline.
- **🗣️ Text-to-speech** — give your assistant a voice with on-device neural voices (Kokoro, Kitten, Supertonic, and Phonon on supported devices) that synthesize speech on your phone, or your phone's system voices.
- **🎙️ Voice input** — dictate messages with on-device Whisper speech recognition (whisper.cpp).
- **🎭 Pals** — create personalized assistants with their own model, system prompt, and personality (Assistant and Roleplay types).
- **🛍️ [PalsHub](https://palshub.ai/)** — discover and install community Pals, including premium ones via in-app purchase.
- **✨ PocketPal Plus** — an optional one-time purchase in the App Store and Google Play builds that adds hands-free voice conversation and a local API server. Builds from source, and the APK on GitHub Releases from the release after v1.23.0, include every Plus feature with no purchase.
- **🛠️ Talents & tools** — let capable Pals call built-in tools (calculator, date/time, rich HTML rendering, opt-in web search and page reading) inside a tool-use loop.
- **📥 Hugging Face integration** — search and download GGUF models, including gated ones, directly from the HF Hub with your access token.
- **📊 Benchmarking** — measure tokens/sec and memory, and optionally compare on the [AI Phone Leaderboard](https://pocketpal.dev/leaderboard).
- **⚡ Hardware acceleration** — CPU, GPU (Metal on iOS, OpenCL/Adreno on Android), and NPU (Qualcomm Hexagon) inference paths, with graceful fallback.
- **🌍 Localized** — available in 16 languages, on phones and tablets, including full iPad support.

## Get the app

| Platform | |
| --- | --- |
| **iOS / iPadOS** | [![Download on the App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App_Store-Download-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pocketpal-ai/id6502579498) |
| **Android** | [![Get it on Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google_Play-Get_it-414141?logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pocketpalai) |

**Three steps to your first chat:**

1. **Install** PocketPal from the App Store or Google Play.
2. **Download a model** — tap the menu (☰) → **Models**, pick one that fits your phone, and download (or add one from Hugging Face).
3. **Load it and start chatting** — that's it, you're running AI fully offline.

## How it works

You don't need to know any of this to use PocketPal — but if you're curious how a phone runs real AI offline, here's the short version.

PocketPal is a four-layer stack, from the silicon up to the chat UI. Each layer has one job, and the dependency direction is strictly top-down — the JS app talks to native bridges, bridges talk to inference engines, engines target hardware backends.

<div align="center">
  <img src="assets/images and logos/stack-diagram-dark.png" alt="PocketPal AI on-device stack — UI & Tool Use → Bridging → Engine → Hardware" width="100%">
</div>

| Layer | What runs here |
| --- | --- |
| **UI & Tool Use** | The React Native app (UI via React Native Paper, state via MobX, chat history in WatermelonDB). The **`AgentRunner`** drives each chat turn — streaming tokens, dispatching **Talents** (tools) when the model calls them, and feeding results back for follow-up reasoning. **Pals** are configurable personas; **PalsHub** is the in-app marketplace for sharing and buying them. In **voice mode**, your speech is transcribed, answered as a normal chat turn, and the reply is spoken back. |
| **Bridging** | Native modules that connect JavaScript to the engines. [`llama.rn`](https://github.com/mybigday/llama.rn) bridges LLM inference over JSI; [`whisper.rn`](https://github.com/mybigday/whisper.rn) bridges speech recognition; [`@pocketpalai/react-native-speech`](https://github.com/a-ghorbani/react-native-speech) and `onnxruntime-react-native` bridge text-to-speech, with the `@pocketpalai/react-native-speech-phonon` add-on for Phonon. |
| **Engine** | The inference engines. **llama.cpp** runs language models in the quantized **GGUF** format. **whisper.cpp** runs Whisper speech recognition models in the **GGML** format. **ONNX Runtime** runs the Kokoro, Kitten and Supertonic voice models in the **ONNX** format. **Phonon** runs natively in its own Rust runtime: a GGUF model on the CPU on Android, a Core ML model on iOS. |
| **Hardware** | Where the math actually happens. PocketPal targets **CPU** (universal fallback), **GPU** (Metal on iOS, OpenCL on Qualcomm Adreno for Android), and **NPU** (Qualcomm Hexagon, and the Apple Neural Engine for Phonon on iOS) — falling back gracefully and offloading partial layers when a full backend isn't available. |

## Using the app

<details>
<summary><strong>📥 Download & load a model</strong></summary>

<br/>

1. Open the app and tap the **Menu** (☰), then go to **Models**.
2. Pick a model from the list and tap **Download**, or tap **+** to add one from Hugging Face or local storage.
3. From Hugging Face, search GGUF models and choose a quantization that fits your device's memory and storage — download now or bookmark for later.
4. After downloading, tap **Load** (or use the chevron icon left of the chat input to load right from the chat screen).

<img src="assets/images and logos/Download_models.png" alt="Download Models" width="100%">
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>💬 Chat</strong></summary>

<br/>

1. Make sure a model is loaded.
2. Open the **Chat** page and start talking.
3. The screen stays awake during inference and deactivates when idle.
4. **Copy** a full response with the copy icon, or long-press a paragraph to copy just that.
5. **Edit** any of your messages with a long-press — the AI regenerates from your change. Hit **retry** for a fresh answer, optionally with a different model.

<img src="assets/images and logos/Chat.png" alt="Chat" width="83%">
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>🎭 Pals & PalsHub</strong></summary>

<br/>

Create personalized assistants:
- **Assistant Pal** — pick a default model, set a system prompt (write it yourself or have the app generate one), and customize the chat input color.
- **Roleplay Pal** — everything above, plus location, the AI's role, and other contextual parameters.

Switch personas with the Pal picker on the chat page. Browse **[PalsHub](https://palshub.ai/)** in-app to discover community Pals, including premium ones via in-app purchase.

<img src="assets/images and logos/Pals.png" alt="Assistant Pal" width="100%">
<p><em>Creating a cocktail-recipe assistant</em></p>
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>📊 Benchmark your device</strong></summary>

<br/>

1. Open the **Benchmark** page.
2. Run performance tests to compare speed and efficiency across models.
3. Review tokens/sec and memory usage.
4. Optionally share your results to the [AI Phone Leaderboard](https://pocketpal.dev/leaderboard).

<img src="assets/images and logos/Benchmark.png" alt="Benchmark" width="100%">
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>🔑 Set up a Hugging Face token (for gated models)</strong></summary>

<br/>

1. Create an access token in your Hugging Face account ([docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/security-tokens)).
2. In PocketPal, go to **Settings → Set Token**, paste it, and save.

<img src="assets/images and logos/Token_in_pocketpal.png" alt="Token setup" width="66%">
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>💌 Send feedback</strong></summary>

<br/>

Go to **App Info → "Sharing your thoughts"**, type your feedback — feature requests, suggestions, anything — and submit.

<img src="assets/images and logos/Send_Feedback.png" alt="Send feedback" width="50%">
</details>

## For developers

PocketPal is a standard React Native app. If you can build a React Native project, you can build PocketPal.

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js** — version is pinned in [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc) (currently `22.21.0`); run `nvm use` to match it. Older Node will fail the `engines` check.
- **Yarn 1 (Classic)** — `packageManager` is pinned to `yarn@1.22.22`.
- **Xcode** + **CocoaPods**, and **Ruby + Bundler** (for iOS / Fastlane tooling).
  - Xcode 26.6 or later, with the Metal Toolchain: `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`.
  - The iOS simulator build needs an Apple silicon Mac.
  - After a change to `patches/llama.rn+*.patch`, remove `node_modules/llama.rn` and run `yarn --check-files` so the patch applies to fresh sources.
- **Android Studio** + Android SDK/NDK.

See the [React Native environment setup](https://reactnative.dev/docs/set-up-your-environment) for platform details.

### Clone, install & run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/a-ghorbani/pocketpal-ai
cd pocketpal-ai

nvm use                       # match the pinned Node version
yarn install                  # install JS dependencies
(cd ios && pod install)       # iOS only

yarn start                    # Metro bundler
yarn ios                      # build + run on iOS simulator
yarn android                  # build + run on Android emulator
```

Core on-device chat works without any backend keys; only PalsHub/auth features need additional configuration.

> **Native-change rule:** if you change `package.json`, a native module, `ios/`, `android/`, the Podfile, or `build.gradle`, re-run `pod install` and rebuild both platforms — a JS reload won't pick up native changes.

### Quality gates

```bash
yarn lint           # ESLint
yarn typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
yarn test           # Jest
yarn l10n:validate  # validate locale JSON (placeholders, integrity)
yarn test:perf      # render-performance tests (Reassure)
yarn test:perf:compare [base]  # render counts of HEAD vs. base (default: merge-base with origin/main)
```

Run `yarn lint && yarn typecheck && yarn test` before opening a PR. Pull requests also run the render-count comparison; see [render-performance tests](docs/render-perf-tests.md). Commits are validated by Commitlint ([Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)) via a Husky hook.

<details>
<summary><strong>Repository layout</strong></summary>

<br/>

```
src/
├── screens/        # Chat, Models, Pals, Benchmark, Settings, Plus, About, …
├── components/     # Reusable UI
├── store/          # MobX stores (Model, ChatSession, Pal, TTS, ASR, VoiceMode, HF, Benchmark, …)
├── services/
│   ├── agent/      # AgentRunner — the chat / tool loop
│   ├── talents/    # Tool engines + registries
│   ├── search/     # Web search providers for the search talents
│   ├── tts/        # TTS engines (kokoro, kitten, supertonic, phonon, system)
│   ├── asr/        # Whisper speech recognition (dictation and voice mode)
│   ├── voice/      # Hands-free voice mode
│   ├── plus/       # Plus feature catalog and gate
│   ├── iap/        # In-app purchases (store bridge)
│   ├── palshub/    # PalsHub marketplace integration
│   ├── deviceRules/ # Device-compatibility rules: parse, classify, launch-time fetch
│   └── downloads/  # Model download manager
├── database/       # WatermelonDB schema, models, migrations
├── repositories/   # Data-access layer over the DB
├── locales/        # i18n JSON + lazy loader (index.ts is the registry)
└── hooks/  api/  theme/  utils/  config/  specs/
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Tech stack</strong></summary>

<br/>

Versions are pinned in [`package.json`](package.json); the highlights:

| Area | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | React Native `0.87.1`, React `19.2.3` (New Architecture) |
| Language | TypeScript `5.9.3` |
| UI | React Native Paper `5.15.3`, React Navigation |
| State | MobX `6` (`mobx`, `mobx-react`, `mobx-persist-store`) |
| Persistence | WatermelonDB (chat history), AsyncStorage (settings), Keychain (secrets) |
| LLM | `llama.rn` `0.13.0-rc.11` → llama.cpp b12292 · GGUF |
| ASR | `whisper.rn` `0.7.4` → whisper.cpp · GGML; mic via `@fugood/react-native-audio-pcm-stream` `1.1.4` |
| TTS | `@pocketpalai/react-native-speech` `2.8.2` + `onnxruntime-react-native` `^1.23.2` · ONNX; `@pocketpalai/react-native-speech-phonon` `0.1.3` |
| Tooling | Yarn 1 (Classic), ESLint, Prettier, Jest, Husky + Commitlint |

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Extending PocketPal</strong></summary>

<br/>

A **Talent** is a tool the model can call mid-conversation. Engines are registered in a `TalentRegistry`, exposed to the model as tool schemas; the `AgentRunner` detects a call, runs the engine, and returns the result for the next turn.

| Talent | Engine | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `calculate` | `CalculateEngine` | Arithmetic / expression evaluation |
| `datetime` | `DatetimeEngine` | Current date / time |
| `render_html` | `RenderHtmlEngine` | Renders model-produced HTML in chat |
| `web_search` | `WebSearchEngine` | Searches the web (opt-in; needs a configured provider) |
| `read_url` | `ReadUrlEngine` | Reads a web page from search results, a site you named, or a link on a page it read (opt-in; needs a configured provider) |

Good first contributions:
- A new **Talent** — implement a `TalentEngine` and register it in `src/services/talents/`.
- A new **TTS engine** — model it on an existing engine in `src/services/tts/engines/`, register it in `engineRegistry.ts`, wire it into `TTSStore`, then search `src/` for that engine's name, ignoring case, to find every other entry it needs, such as its type, constants, setup-sheet entries and strings.
- A new **locale** — translate on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/pocketpal-ai/); registering a new language in the app follows the steps in `src/locales/index.ts`.

</details>

## Contributing

M3E Canvas is a free, open-source sketchpad for app screens made of real Material 3 Expressive parts. It runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server, nothing to install. What you sketch becomes a precise prompt that any AI coding tool that takes one, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor, can turn into a working app.

<p align="center"><a href="https://lnkiai.github.io/m3e-canvas/"><img src="docs/readme/ui/open-en.png" height="56" alt="Open the app" /></a></p>

## <img src="docs/readme/ui/icon-how.png" width="32" height="32" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> How it works

<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 767px)" srcset="docs/readme/cards/how-narrow.png" />
  <img src="docs/readme/cards/how-wide.png" alt="The three steps: building a screen from the parts panel, tapping through it in the preview, and copying the prompt" />
</picture>

1. **Sketch** — Drag parts onto phone or desktop screens. They snap together and line up on a 4dp grid.
2. **Tap through** — Link parts to screens and press Preview to try the flow, transitions included.
3. **Copy the prompt** — The whole design becomes a short brief in your language. Paste it into your AI coding tool.

## <img src="docs/readme/ui/icon-features.png" width="32" height="32" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> What's inside

<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 767px)" srcset="docs/readme/cards/features-narrow.png" />
  <img src="docs/readme/cards/features-wide.png" alt="Four features: a part's own panel, linked screens, the colors panel and the Ask an AI dialog" />
</picture>

<img src="docs/readme/ui/feature-parts.png" width="24" height="24" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Real M3 Expressive parts** — Buttons, FABs, bars, tabs, cards, lists, sheets, pickers, carousels, loading indicators and more, each with its own panel for text, style, size and what a tap does.

<img src="docs/readme/ui/feature-flow.png" width="24" height="24" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Screens and flow** — Phone and desktop screens, screens that scroll, taps and swipes that open other screens with the transition you pick, and arrows that show the whole flow.

<img src="docs/readme/ui/feature-theme.png" width="24" height="24" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Theme in one place** — Color, shape, type and motion: seven palettes or your own seed color, light and dark, three contrast levels, corner styles, fonts and the expressive spring motion.

<img src="docs/readme/ui/feature-ai.png" width="24" height="24" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Optional AI help** — Bring your own key to draft a design or write notes for you, or copy an instruction for a coding agent that replies with a share link. Keys never leave your browser.

<details>
<summary><b>Everything it can do</b></summary>

- **Parts** – buttons, icon buttons, FABs and extended FABs, FAB menus, split buttons, chips, top app bars, navigation bars and rails, floating toolbars, tabs, search bars, cards, list items, boxes, bottom sheets, dialogs, snackbars, text fields, dropdowns, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders, date and time pickers, text, images, carousels, camera and map placeholders, dividers, the shape-morphing loading indicator and wavy progress indicators. Every part has a panel for its text, style, size and alignment, and a trigger tab for what a tap does.
- **Magnetic connections** – bring buttons, chips or list items close and they fuse into a connected group; the corners soften where they meet.
- **Phone and desktop screens** – add as many screens as you like. Switch any screen between a 412×892 phone and a 1280×800 desktop from its label: bars stretch, a navigation bar becomes a rail and back again, and the parts are laid out again. Same-named screens are written into the prompt as one screen at two widths.
- **Screens that scroll** – make a screen longer than its device and its body scrolls under the bars in the preview. Drag the grip on the bottom bezel, or pick 1x to 3x in the screen panel.
- **Tap and swipe to navigate** – give any tappable part, app bar icon or navigation destination a target screen (or "back") and a transition: slide from any side, fade, expand or none. Screens can also open others on a swipe. The preview plays it all, and back runs in reverse.
- **Layers and groups** – a layers panel per screen to change the stacking order; group parts to keep their overlap and move them as one, then copy and paste whole selections across screens.
- **Theme** – seven palettes or one seed color that becomes a full Material 3 scheme you can fine-tune, light and dark, three contrast levels and dynamic color. Square, rounded or full corners for every part at once. Roboto, Roboto Flex, Roboto Serif or the system font. The standard or the expressive spring motion, which also drives the preview.
- **Prompt** – the whole design or a single screen as a concise brief in Japanese, English, Chinese or Korean, with your notes on what each part does. Rows, overlaps and aligned grids of cards are spelled out, so the generated layout keeps them. Choose Android or the web as the target, edit the text before copying, or save a screen as a PNG.
- **Tidy** – one button snaps bars to the edges and the FAB to the corner, joins neighbouring items, and stacks the rest on 16dp margins. Press it again to undo.
- **AI helper (optional)** – bring your own key for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek to draft a design from a sentence or write a part's behaviour note and a screen's description. Every rewrite can be undone. The request goes straight from your browser to the provider.
- **Share links** – copy a link that opens your design on anyone's canvas, or an instruction for Claude Code, Codex or another agent: it reads [agent.md](public/agent.md), sketches what you described, and replies with such a link.
- **Everything else** – alignment guides and a 4dp grid, undo and redo, keyboard shortcuts, a keyboard-usable parts panel, favorites, install as an app, and autosave in your browser.
- **On a phone** – one fixed screen and a buttons-only editor with bottom sheets. The full editor is for desktop browsers.

</details>

## <img src="docs/readme/ui/icon-keyboard.png" width="32" height="32" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `V` / `H` | Select / hand tool (hold `Space` to pan) |
| Wheel, `Ctrl` + wheel | Pan, zoom |
| `+` `-` `0` | Zoom in, zoom out, fit |
| `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo |
| `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy / paste parts, also across screens |
| `Ctrl+D` | Duplicate |
| `Ctrl+G` / `Ctrl+Shift+G` | Group / ungroup |
| `Shift` + click | Add to the selection |
| Arrows (`Shift` = 8dp) | Nudge |
| `Ctrl` + drag | Move without snapping (no guides, no 4dp grid) |
| `Delete` | Delete part or screen |
| `P` | Preview |

## <img src="docs/readme/ui/icon-run.png" width="32" height="32" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
npm run build      # static export to ./out
```

The app is a static Next.js export. To host it under a sub-path (for example a GitHub Pages project site), set `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/your-repo` at build time. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` does this and publishes `out/` to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`.
